page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.16-128 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine configuration belonging to the Standard family. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9J14 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading at a clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

In terms of hardware peripheral allocation, the instance does not feature dedicated graphics processing units and bundles no local storage. Persistent storage requirements rely entirely on attached network block volumes. Network configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address for external access.

From an architectural perspective, the provision of dedicated CPU cores ensures consistent compute availability without hypervisor oversubscription. Given the balanced compute and memory allocation without local storage acceleration, the hardware profile fits multi-threaded enterprise software runtimes, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and general application serving workloads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance providing a balanced compute and memory profile. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, delivering 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB allocation per vCPU. No integrated local storage drives are bundled with the hardware, requiring attached remote block storage volumes for persistence, and it contains zero discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported with one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated compute resources and a steady memory-to-core ratio, this shape supports mid-tier enterprise software, web application servers, container management nodes, CI/CD pipelines, and general business logic processing.
